title: Family 3
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. Two risks here, not one. The first is the usual predecessor overlap — a1_home_family (30) and a2_family (25) own the whole nuclear set. The second is NEWER and would not have shown up in a naive draft: b2_relationships, four units earlier on the same path, already took the family-structure words (stepfather, half-brother, custody, adoption, foster, in-laws). So this unit deliberately does not repeat family SHAPES at all. Its angle is where a family comes from and what it hands on: origins (ancestor, ancestry, descendant, heritage, family tree, resemblance, take after), what passes down (inheritance, heir, legacy, next of kin, guardian, widow, orphan), and the shapes of growing up (parenthood, generation gap, sibling rivalry, only child, single parent, role model, breadwinner). The sweep dropped inherit, raise, bring up, spoil, generation and in-laws as already taught. C57 card 0 recaps Family 1 and 2. C49 all 36 words across three boards of 12. Build-the-family card is half recap: inherit and parent are words the student already has, and this unit adds inheritance and parenthood; ancestor -> ancestry and resemble -> resemblance run inside the unit. All four derived forms are bank items and use the -ance/-hood/-ry endings b2_suffixes_1 teaches. A12 senses: heritage (cultural) vs inheritance (property) are kept apart on the Czech side, and discipline (of children) is marked because the school-subject reading is the commoner one. Bands 2 B2 / 4 C1 / 30 unbanded, the b2_home profile — kinship vocabulary sits largely outside the Oxford 5k. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Family 1 and 2 gave you the people in the room — mother, father, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, cousin, grandparent — and the words around them: couple, adult, kid, relative, wedding, birth, background, community. Those words come back in this unit's sentences. What is new here is the family seen across time: where it came from, what it hands on, and the shapes it actually takes.
cards.note_cz: Family 1 a 2 ti daly lidi v místnosti — mother, father, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, cousin, grandparent — a slova kolem nich: couple, adult, kid, relative, wedding, birth, background, community. Ta slova se vracejí ve větách. Nové je tu rodina v čase: odkud přišla, co předává a jaké podoby doopravdy má.

cards.title: Build the family
points: The first two you already know — here are the nouns built on them.
**-ance**, **-hood** and **-ry** do the building, as in Suffixes 2.
